data.body:
Second independent occurrence confirms the root cause, and rules out a narrow submit-race reading.

Run `35492165781`:

- Run created `2026-09-20T05:37:56Z`; `actions/checkout` therefore ran at about `05:38:0x`.
- Gerrit change **2994** (`Stop the cap handler lying about a dry-run`) was submitted at **`05:38:16`** — a few seconds AFTER that checkout.
- The merged-reachability check failed at **`05:43:21`**, five minutes later, with the same
  `Gerrit/GitHub main diverged or Gerrit MERGED revisions are not reachable from main.`
- The next scheduled run passed with no intervention.

The five-minute gap is the decisive detail. A pure replication-lag race would have cleared
long before `05:43:21`; GitHub `main` had certainly received 2994 by then. What had NOT
changed is the job's own `HEAD`, frozen at checkout time `05:38:0x` — before 2994 landed.

So the failing comparison is not "Gerrit ahead of GitHub". It is "Gerrit ahead of a GitHub
snapshot this job took minutes ago". That isolates defect 2 in the description — the stale
`destination_ref="HEAD"` baseline — as the dominant cause, with the missing re-sample
(defect 1) removing the only mechanism that could have absorbed it.

Both observed failures fit: run `35497408797` had a 10-second gap (2997 at `07:41:48`,
error at `07:41:58`), run `35492165781` had a five-minute gap. A fix that only added
re-sampling without re-fetching the GitHub tip would still fail the second case, because
re-sampling a frozen `HEAD` returns the same answer every time.
